title: Do Verifiers Reduce Security-Relevant Misconfigurations? A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Verifier-in-the-Loop GVR for Intent-to-Configuration
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired evaluation to test whether embedding a reachability/policy verifier inside a generate–verify–repair (GVR) loop reduces the incidence of security-increasing (forbidden-reachability) misconfigurations produced by an LLM-driven intent→configuration pipeline. Using Dockerized FRRouting-style emulation, two deterministic validators (a containerized Batfish instance and a Python graph-based static reachability analyzer), and a matched sample of N=300 intents (150 benign + 150 programmatic adversarial variants), we compared single-pass LLM generation (baseline) to an LLM+verifier GVR pipeline implemented with gpt-5-mini under a preregistered protocol (study cnd-2026-netops-gvr-security-01-prereg-v1). The execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one LLM draw shared between baseline and guarded per pair), producing one LLM call per pair (model_calls_used = 300). The run completed the planned 600 episodes with zero failed episodes. The confirmatory outcome was degenerate: baseline_success = 300 and guarded_success = 300 (contingency n11=300, n10=n01=n00=0). Paired risk-difference = 0.0, exact McNemar p = 1.0, 95% bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Crucially, validators never reported forbidden reachability and the GVR repair step was never invoked; thus the experiment evaluates whether inserting a verifier changes observed compliance when baseline generation already meets the safety predicate, not whether verifier-guided repair can rescue genuine violations. We report artifact-backed execution and analysis results and discuss design choices that explain the null and guide future stress-testing.

sections.introduction: Automating intent-driven network configuration with large language models (LLMs) promises operational speedups but raises real safety concerns: generated configurations can introduce unintended reachability, violate access-control policies, or otherwise expand attack surface. Prior system and survey work therefore recommends integrating execution oracles and generate–verify–repair (GVR) loops to detect and correct hazardous outputs. However, the operational efficacy of verifier-in-the-loop designs—specifically their capacity to reduce security-increasing misconfigurations under adversarial intents—remains incompletely quantified. We pose a focused confirmatory question and test it under a preregistered paired design: Does embedding a reachability/policy verifier inside a GVR loop reduce the incidence of forbidden-reachability misconfigurations produced by an LLM-driven intent→configuration pipeline? Our contributions are (1) a machine-readable preregistration (study id cnd-2026-netops-gvr-security-01-prereg-v1) that fixes a paired N=300 design and analysis plan; (2) a fully deterministic Dockerized execution that uses FRRouting-style router images and two independent validators; and (3) complete execution and analysis artifacts showing that, for the selected task set, model (gpt-5-mini), and execution contract (shared_initial_candidate), baseline single-pass generation already satisfied the forbidden-reachability predicate on every pair, so inserting the verifier produced no measurable improvement.
sections.related_work: Three strands motivated our design. First, GVR and execution-guided repair architectures improve correctness on many code and IaC tasks, but gains vary by task, verifier, and model; representative system papers include TerraFormer and other recent verifier-feedback studies. Second, surveys and NetOps studies document LLM failure modes—hallucination, overconfidence, and domain mismatch—and recommend validators, constrained generation, or human oversight. Third, emulation and testbed work demonstrates that execution-based validation is feasible in research settings but warns that external validity (production networks, live traffic) is limited. Our experiment sits at the intersection: an execution-validated, preregistered paired test that targets an operationally meaningful safety predicate (forbidden reachability) rather than raw language-quality metrics. All cited records were verified during the autonomous literature pass and are listed in the bibliography.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The preregistered study (cnd-2026-netops-gvr-security-01-prereg-v1) specified a paired design with primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (absolute difference in proportion of intents yielding forbidden reachability). Sampling used a fixed matched sample N=300 (150 benign seeds and 150 adversarial variants produced programmatically from each benign seed). Intervention and execution contract: for each matched intent we executed (A) baseline: single-pass LLM generation (one LLM call), and (B) guarded: initial LLM generation + verifier check + up to one repair LLM call (GVR). The preregistration froze the GVR repair policy: a repair prompt is issued only if a validator reports forbidden reachability; at most one repair call is permitted per pair. The execution contract adopted shared_initial_candidate semantics: a single initial LLM candidate was generated and re-used for both baseline and guarded playback; this decision conserved model calls but reduces the opportunity for independent-condition discordance (model_calls_used = 300 for 300 pairs). Validators and scoring rule: two deterministic validators were used: (i) a containerized Batfish instance and (ii) a Python graph-based static reachability analyzer. An episode was declared to exhibit forbidden reachability if either validator reported the forbidden-reachability predicate (equivalently, an episode is a 'success' only if neither validator reports a violation). Per-episode validator traces record validator_id='deterministic_netops_validator_v5' and validator_version='5.0' (see representative scoring traces such as execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json). Detailed validator artifacts (Batfish container image, Batfish policy filenames, and the Python analyzer implementation and file SHA-256) are archived in the evidence bundle; consult execution/execution_manifest.json in the archived artifacts for the exact identifiers. Environment and determinism: the experiment ran in Docker compositions using FRRouting-style router images; all orchestration, seeds, and deterministic sampling parameters were preregistered. Analysis plan and prespecified deviation: primary confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two-sided paired test (alpha=0.05) on N=300 pairs, with 95% bootstrap percentile confidence intervals computed from resampling. The preregistration planned 1,000 bootstrap resamples; the final analysis used 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed=1729) to reduce Monte Carlo error. This change is recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (artifact in the evidence bundle) and is reported here.
sections.results: Execution accounting: the adapter completed all planned episodes (600 = 300 pairs × 2 conditions), used model_calls_used = 300 (maximum_model_calls allowed = 600 under the preregistered adapter contract), and recorded zero failed episodes (deterministic_reconciliation.json). Primary outcome: complete_pair_count = 300; baseline_success_count = 300; guarded_success_count = 300. Paired contingency: n11 = 300, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Paired risk-difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] computed from 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). Repair activity: under the preregistered GVR logic a repair would be attempted only when a validator reported forbidden reachability; across the entire run validators never reported forbidden reachability for any initial candidate, so no repair prompts were generated and no repair calls were applied (per-episode validator_trace fields show repair_applied=false and repair_prompt_sha256=null for representative episodes such as execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json). Model-call overhead: because of the shared_initial_candidate contract, provider-call audit records stage_counts 'shared_initial_generation' = 300 and median guarded-model-call overhead = 0. Concordance of validators: per-episode validator traces show no violations reported by either validator across all pairs, and no inter-verifier disagreement was observed (verifier_disagreement_rate = 0 by episode traces). Artifact pointers and verification: key archived artifacts and their SHA-256 hashes (as recorded in the evidence bundle) include execution/raw_results.jsonl (36ea4a5dfa90384f2a388cba4f39bf193bb3c150ea22ca60957facb20ca960f1), execution/model_configuration.json (a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (62bd1fe90a9ad7b2798d5241c3c52404750cbab678e6b92692d2cc2bae2356bf), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (a39fd3386c945cae095f2f310ead1f21ac600f8b2492bcd49b664c8da5782aa0), analysis/condition_summary.csv (4583b822df7318438acf50085740c33d5972dff92bc2a0f077795ba8cfb950eb), and deterministic_reconciliation.json (d5f2a8d1a1ebb7f4494b66533e3d4cb3bb21fbc85696a155787a3a82c4d25ea9). These artifact paths and hashes enable verification of the reported numbers without reproducing low-level provenance lists in the main text.
sections.discussion: Interpretation and causes of the degenerate null: the confirmatory result is degenerate because the baseline already satisfied the forbidden-reachability predicate for all preregistered tasks; with zero discordant pairs the paired test is uninformative about repair efficacy. Two preregistered design choices explain this outcome. First, the shared_initial_candidate contract (one shared LLM draw per pair) conserves model calls but reduces independent-condition variance that might create discordant violating outputs; provider-call audit records 'shared_initial_generation' = 300. Second, the adversarial-variant generator used here did not produce verifier-detectable forbidden reachability given the chosen model and validators. Operational implications: results show that inserting a verifier will not change observed compliance when the baseline already complies; demonstrating verifier utility therefore requires experimental contracts that exercise the repair path. Recommendations for future stress-testing experiments: (1) adopt independent-condition generation or increase repair-call budgets so repair paths can be exercised; (2) strengthen adversarial-intent generation (algorithmic adversaries targeting verifier predicates) to raise baseline violation rates; (3) evaluate multiple LLM families and stronger oracles; and (4) include production-representative device heterogeneity and live-traffic conditions when safety claims are operational. Threats to validity: internal validity concerns include prompt sensitivity and the shared-generation contract; construct validity concerns include whether the forbidden-reachability predicate and the chosen validators capture the operational security risk of interest; external validity is limited by the synthetic task bank, single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini), and Dockerized FRRouting-style emulation. All of these threats are described in the Limitations section and in the archived preregistration and manifest.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired evaluation of a verifier-in-the-loop GVR pipeline for intent→configuration generation using gpt-5-mini over 300 matched intents. The confirmatory outcome was degenerate: both baseline and guarded conditions passed the forbidden-reachability predicate on all pairs (n11=300). Because the verifier never reported violations, the repair path was never invoked and the study cannot assess whether GVR repairs would rescue genuine violations. This result highlights that experimental-contract choices—generation semantics (shared vs independent), adversarial potency, repair budget, verifier strength, and model diversity—materially determine whether verifier-in-the-loop architectures can demonstrate benefits in NetOps security. We therefore recommend follow-up studies that intentionally exercise repair paths via stronger adversaries, independent-condition generation, multi-model comparisons, and more diverse execution oracles.

limitations: Degenerate confirmatory outcome: zero discordant pairs (n11=300, n10=n01=n00=0) render McNemar inference uninformative about repair efficacy when baseline violation rates are nonzero; the preregistered power calculation assumed a nonzero baseline violation rate and targeted detecting a 30 percentage-point absolute reduction.

GVR not exercised: under the chosen task set, emulator, and validators the verifier never reported forbidden reachability and consequently the guarded repair step was never invoked; the experiment therefore tests whether verifier insertion changes compliance when baseline is already compliant, not whether verifier-guided repair rescues violations.

Generation contract choice: the preregistered shared_initial_generation semantics produced one LLM call per pair and reduced model-call overhead but also limited independent draws that could produce discordant errors; alternative contracts (independent-condition generation or expanded repair budgets) would better exercise repair paths.

External validity: tasks were synthetically generated and executed in Dockerized FRRouting-style emulation; results do not necessarily generalize to heterogeneous production devices, live traffic conditions, or different operational constraints.
Model and verifier scope: a single model (gpt-5-mini) and two deterministic validators were evaluated; other LLMs, stronger verifiers, or dynamic execution oracles may produce different outcomes.

Validator artifacts and low-level container tags: precise Batfish container-image tags/digests and the exact Batfish policy file names and Python analyzer file SHA-256 are preserved in the archived execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) but are not printed inline here to keep the manuscript concise; readers can retrieve those exact identifiers from the archived manifest.
